entities.summary: John of Damascus or John Damascene, born Yūḥana ibn Manṣūr ibn Sarjūn, was a Christian monk, priest, hymnographer, and apologist. He was born and raised in Damascus c. AD 675 or AD 676; the precise date and place of his death is not known, though tradition places it at his monastery, Mar Saba, near Jerusalem, on 4 December AD 749. A polymath whose fields of interest and contribution included law, theology, philosophy, and music, he was given the by-name of Chrysorroas. He wrote works expounding the Christian faith, and composed hymns which are still used both liturgically in Eastern Christian practice throughout the world as well as in western Lutheranism at Easter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a polymath and apologist, John of Damascus's hymns continue to be used in both Eastern Christian practice and western Lutheranism at Easter, with his works expounding the Christian faith influencing theological discourse for centuries. His contributions reflect significant regional impact within the early medieval period.
